A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fiddler and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and reorganization, supporting comparison despite the substantial revision.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Mixtral inference benchmarks. Appendices A-C report activation sparsity, CPU/GPU microbenchmarks, and expert-selection measurements.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original generation, long-prefill, and beam-search benchmarks. The appendices additionally report dataset sensitivity, Phi-3.5-MoE performance, and latency breakdowns.

M1.justification: The reported scheduling rule changes substantially. V1 Section 3.2 jointly partitions experts to minimize the maximum aggregate CPU/GPU latency; v2 Algorithm 1 independently assigns each uncached expert by comparing CPU latency against GPU computation plus weight-transfer latency. Popularity-based initial placement already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V2 extends short-input ShareGPT generation evaluation to long-context prefilling and beam-search generation, introducing substantially different workload requirements. Appendix D also adds LMSYS-Chat-1M as a second conversation corpus.

E2.justification: V2 adds llama.cpp to the main comparison alongside the retained DeepSpeed-MII and Mixtral-Offloading, plotted as Eliseev & Mazur. This introduces an important CPU-based competitor missing from v1's offloading-only comparisons. Llama.cpp also supplies the beam-search comparison.

E3.justification: Environment 2 changes from L4 with a 32-core CPU to RTX 6000 Ada with a 112-core CPU, with revised expert residency and offloading settings. V2 changes sequence-length configurations and adds TTFT/ITL measurements, beam widths 4-16, and Phi-3.5-MoE evaluation. Its exact main length grid is inconsistent: Section 4.1 specifies four input and four output lengths, while Figure 4 plots five input and three output lengths.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds an input-distribution sensitivity study comparing conversation datasets, and Appendix F separates prefill and decoding latency through TTFT/ITL breakdowns. These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence. The sparsity and expert-popularity analyses are retained, while microbenchmarks and hardware-dependent popularity calculations are revised.

E5.justification: V1 specifies averaging 10 runs for Fiddler and three for baselines; v2 omits these end-to-end repetition counts. Both retain 32 microbenchmark executions with means and standard deviations. This is a limited loss of statistical reporting, without evidence that the actual repetition counts decreased.

E6.justification: V1 reports 8.2x/10.1x speedups over Mixtral-Offloading in its two environments. V2 reports 1.26x over llama.cpp across revised environments, 11.57x for beam search, and 6.5x over DeepSpeed-MII for Phi-3.5-MoE, alongside new sensitivity and latency-breakdown results. These are new or replaced comparisons, not matched-setting performance changes. Microbenchmark and Environment 2 hit-rate results also change; Table 2's sparsity values remain identical.

T1.justification: V1's central min-max optimization over disjoint CPU/GPU expert sets, justified by parallel completion time, is removed. V2 substitutes an expert-wise latency inequality with separate GPU computation and transfer costs. This substantively changes the formal scheduling model, while retaining the linear-CPU and constant-GPU latency assumptions. Neither version provides an optimality proof.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contribution on running uncompressed Mixtral on 24GB GPUs with large single-batch gains over offloading systems. V2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the central claim to adaptive heterogeneous execution outperforming specialized competitors across ordinary generation, long prefills, and beam search.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of the complementary strengths of CPU-based and offloading baselines, and interprets Appendix D/E results as evidence of distribution robustness and applicability beyond Mixtral. The underlying communication/computation explanation, compression compatibility, and assumption that non-expert weights fit on the GPU remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds baseline version numbers, llama.cpp ngl settings, specific CPU models, initialization-time latency profiling, and disclosure of an AVX512_BF16 expert kernel. V1's explicit non-persistent DeepSpeed pipeline statement disappears. These are bounded changes in implementation and reproducibility documentation; the PyTorch basis and code-access URL remain.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises positioning by acknowledging CPU-based hybrid inference, particularly llama.cpp, and distinguishing Fiddler through adaptive execution rather than CPU computation alone. Related work and motivation expand to newer MoE models, heterogeneous deployment, long-context applications, and additional inference systems.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, design explanation, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Design is reorganized into overview, execution strategies, algorithm, and optimizations, with explicit contribution bullets. The original sparsity and microbenchmark appendices exchange order, and new appendices D-F are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds high-level and initialization/execution diagrams, redraws v1 Figure 1 as a three-case execution diagram, and introduces an algorithm display plus multiple benchmark and diagnostic panels. Existing plots are also redesigned. The sparsity table and popularity heatmap are retained. Several v2 plot legends inconsistently call the proposed system Twiddler while captions use Fiddler.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's evaluation: it adds the stronger CPU-based llama.cpp comparator and tests workloads that expose different execution tradeoffs. Dataset sensitivity, a second MoE model, and latency breakdowns substantially strengthen evidence for applicability and performance. Omitted end-to-end run counts and setup/plot inconsistencies weaken reproducibility and clarity, but the broader, more relevant comparative evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
